groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
M: OK then, this here is your yearly performance review. You've been with the company for 3 years and under my direct supervision for the past 12 months. Your report is mostly good. But there are a couple of issues we must discuss. The report is yours to take with you. We'll go through the main points together now. And you can come through it in greater detail later. Do you have any questions before we start?
W: No, sir.
M: I'll get straight to it then. It is evident that you are a hard worker. You are punctual and industrious. Furthermore, you have strong analytical skills and attention to detail. The company, myself included, is happy with your productivity and overall performance.
W: Thank you. I appreciate the recognition.
M: Do you agree, then, with this depiction so far?
W: Yeah, it's a little simplistic perhaps. But that's to be expected from this kind of evaluation.
M: Sure. Would you want to add anything? Your comments can be added to the report if you wish.
W: Oh, there's no need. It's a flattering portrayal really. Thank you, though.
M: OK. This leads me to the not-so-good part. This mostly centers around one behavioral aspect—your ability to work with others.
W: I see.
M: Yes. As you already know, over the last several months, there have been some complaints raised about your communication style.
W: Of course, we already had like three meetings about this. Look, all I'm going to say is that it was never my intention to offend anyone. Simply put, I don't like to write long emails, because, frankly, I think they're a waste of time. Conciseness is efficiency. I feel that writing long emails hurts that same productivity you praised me for just a minute ago. And I already apologized if anyone was offended. But to be perfectly honest, I think anyone who was offended was being a little too sensitive.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
M: So tell me, why do you wish to study medicine?
W: I've always wanted to be a doctor. I come from a small town where healthcare was never the best. And I think that had a profound effect on me. As a child, I remember thinking how great it would be to serve the community and cure people!
M: What other people or events in your life have shaped your interest in becoming a doctor?
W: Well, that's hard to say. I would certainly say my parents have been a key factor. They always pushed me to study hard. And I certainly wouldn't be here without their support. I guess I was also immensely fortunate to have good teachers and friends around me. At the end of the day, I've always been surrounded by a positive environment conducive to my working hard and pursuing my dreams.
M: Is there any medical branch that you would like to specialize in?
W: I haven't decided yet. It's still early days. However, if I had to say, internal medicine.
M: Why internal medicine?
W: I know it's no picnic. But I find it the most intriguing, because it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties.
M: Thank you. Now I'd like to address your academic history and projected grades. We like to think of ourselves as a prestigious institution with a highly competitive and promising student body. As you know, to get into our programmes, you need at least 85% score in the entrance exam. Do you think you can attain this?
W: I think so. Yes.
M: I'm looking at your school grades now and I'll be honest. It's a bit of a mixed bag. You do get top grades here and there, but you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"? I see no problem in making you a conditional offer, but consider yourself warned, our entrance exam is, to use your own words, no picnic.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Logging into your email account can sometimes feel like trying to hack into the Pentagon. If you follow all of the guidelines, you need to use a different password for every one of your accounts; use an incomprehensible variety of letters, numbers, and symbols; sign up for two-step verification; and change every password every time one of them is compromised. More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being.
It's no small wonder most of us forget our passwords more often than our keys. Now a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon. Their findings suggest that how likely you are to remember your password has less to do with the password itself and more to do with how often you anticipate using it. Which is to say: you are far more likely to remember a complicated password if you know you'll frequently be using it to log into an account than you are to remember a simple password for an account that you don't expect to log into very often. The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often in order to help them remember their secret codes.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material: Four years ago, Jenny Weiner was in a fitness slump. She wanted to improve her physical and mental health. However, her workouts lacked intensity without a proper training programme to follow. When she went to the gym, her daily ritual predominantly involved easy exercise options like jogging; she avoided more formidable exercises like lifting weights. A personal trainer who might push her was out of the question. The extravagant cost was just unaffordable. She then discovered the fitness phone app Slimmeretics. To use the app, you first input your profile about your previous training experiences and preferences, as well as your desired goals. A virtual coach then uses that information to suggest a personalised training regime. After the workout, the app's artificial intelligence software system gives feedback from Ms. Weiner and its other 53 million users around the world to adjust future training sessions. Now Ms. Weiner finds the workouts exciting. This is because no two are ever the same. As a result, the app has helped her to lose more than 25 kilograms. The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule. This has led to optimal results. However, some experts think that apps cannot replace human personal trainers. An app cannot understand human behavior. It will not comprehend that there are competing interests outside of health and fitness. Additionally, a human trainer can add compassion to the workout. He can also make exercise fun and sustainable. Trainers can monitor whether a person is doing exercises correctly. This can safeguard against injuries. An app cannot perceive such subtleties.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded. Although many cultures are moving towards more liberal, less hierarchical organizations, the new research suggests that traditional power structures and basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies.
The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes. Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favors, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly, and respect the property of others. The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilized society and foster social cooperation, researchers found. "Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code," said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford. "These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures, because people face the same social problems. Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something. This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us."
The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality. The team accessed the world's best archives to analyze accounts from more than 600 sources of 60 societies around the world. They found that the seven rules were considered morally good in all societies and were observed across all continents, religions and politics. However, some communities valued certain rules more highly than others. Dr. Curry hopes that this research helps to promote mutual understanding between people of different cultures and appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ. Co-author professor Harvey Whitehouse said social scientists should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data. "This study was based on historical descriptions of cultures around the world," he said. "These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing. In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field."

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
When it comes to food, color is money. Food companies know that better color gives better prices, so they ensure that their products are attractive in color to bolster earnings. Oranges, for example, have to meet specific color standards. And oranges are just the beginning. There are color standards for foods including French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey and cherries.
The attention to color is for good reason. For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience. A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision, while only a percent or two is given over to taste faculties, and the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.
Scientists have demonstrated many times the importance of color to taste. In a 1980s study, for example, test participants were asked to name the flavor of the beverage they were drinking without being able to see that beverage. Only one in five was able to identify it as orange. But when they were allowed to see what they were drinking which was orange in color, each of them identified the orange flavor. And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of respondents identified the flavor of the beverage as orange. None made that mistake when the beverage was green in color. What's happening when someone fails to identify the flavor of a beverage they can't see or that has an abnormal color? Is it that participants can't discern what the flavor is, and so rely on visual cues? Or does color actually change the experience of taste? The key to these questions is the effect of color on expectation. The brain makes predictions using color. These predictions rely on expectations that come from experience. Research shows that we're all born liking sweet things and desire to eat them, but we aren't born knowing what the sweet things we crave look like. So we need to learn this over time. The brain gets information from the environment. And we learn, for example, that fruits go from green and sour to red and ripe and sweet. Thus, if we see a green berry, we equate its color with a sour taste, and just looking at a red fruit will activate our expectations that it will taste sweet and delicious.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives. For some, this meaning is religious, some political and some interpersonal. And having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness.
A new study looks at the relationship between meaning and happiness in the context of financial resources. Rhea Catapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people, suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning. The team analysed data from over 500,000 people across 123 countries. The first study used data from a daily poll of US residents collected between 2013 and 2015. Well-being was tracked using measures of positive affect—whether, during the day before they were surveyed, participants had smiled or laughed a lot or experienced a lot of happiness. Meaning was measured through a daily "purpose index", which explored the extent to which participants felt that they like what they do every day and are motivated to achieve their goals. Finally, income levels were assessed. The results showed that the correlation between meaning and happiness was strongest among those in lower income brackets. But as income levels increased, the correlation became weaker. The second study looked at worldwide data. Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study, while meaning was measured using the single question: "Do you feel your life has an important purpose or meaning?" Again, the strength of the relationship between meaning and happiness depended on participants' income: meaning had a greater influence on happiness for those on lower incomes compared to those in higher brackets. In the final study, French participants indicated the extent to which they felt they led a purposeful and meaningful life and how much they considered themselves a happy person. Finally, rather than using specific income brackets, they placed themselves on a "social ladder", representing where they stand in society with regard to wealth, education, and career. The results from the study duplicated those of the first two.
So overall, meaning and happiness had a stronger relationship in those with fewer resources than those with more. This might be the case because rich individuals have more access to other sources of happiness—many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community. Thus, a focus on an internal sense of satisfaction, purpose or meaning is less important.

questions.prompt: What are the speakers most probably doing?
options: Preparing for a job interview.
Writing a work report together.
Going through a couple of issues the company faces.
Discussing the woman's annual performance review.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are the speakers most probably doing? 

 【翻译】 说话者最有可能在做什么? 
 A)  准备工作面试。 
 B)  一起撰写工作报告。 
 C)  梳理公司面临的几个问题。 
 D)  讨论女士的年度绩效评估。 

 【答案】 D （主旨题） Discussing the woman's annual performance review. 
 【定位】 P1 OK then, this here is your yearly performance review. You've been with the company for 3 years and under my direct supervision for the past 12 months. 
 那好，这是你的年度绩效评估。你在公司已经三年，过去十二个月在我的直接管理之下。 

 【信号】 开头场景定调句 。对话第一句 this here is your yearly performance review 就开门见山点出场合，是典型的“开头定调”信号：主旨情境题的答案往往就埋在第一句对场合的交代里。 

 【替换】 this here is your yearly performance review ↔ Discussing the woman's annual performance review yearly等于annual 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音是上司给在职三年的下属做评估，全程没有应聘、招人的内容，Preparing for a job interview. 凭“职场”联想硬套，属未提及。 
 B) 原词陷阱 录音里 report 是指已经写好的评估报告(Your report is mostly good)，男方说 the report is yours to take，并非两人“一起写报告”。Writing a work report together. 盗用了原词 report 却把“一起过报告”偷换成“一起写报告”。  借用原文：Your report is mostly good 

 C) 原词陷阱 男方确实说了 there are a couple of issues we must discuss，但那只是这次绩效面谈的一部分(后半段才谈问题)，并非两人整体“只在过几个公司问题”。Going through a couple of issues the company faces. 盗用 a couple of issues 把局部当成了全局，且 issues 是关于“她”的，不是“公司面临的问题”。  借用原文：there are a couple of issues we must discuss

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she appreciates?
options: The overall culture of the company.
The instruction from her supervisor.
The honesty of the manager.
The recognition of her merits.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say she appreciates? 

 【翻译】 女士说她欣赏什么? 
 A)  公司的整体文化。 
 B)  主管的指导。 
 C)  经理的诚实。 
 D)  对她优点的认可。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The recognition of her merits. 
 【定位】 P4 Thank you. I appreciate the recognition. 
 谢谢，我很感激这份认可。 

 【信号】 被问者的直接应答 。男方刚夸完她勤奋、有分析力、令公司满意，女方紧接着应答 I appreciate the recognition，这句“道谢 + appreciate”正是与题干 appreciate 直接对应的应答句，信号极明确。 

 【替换】 I appreciate the recognition ↔ The recognition of her merits. 认可即对优点的认可 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 The overall culture of the company. 录音从未谈“公司文化”，只是借 company 一词(男方多次提 the company)制造“职场”联想，属未提及。 
 B) 原词陷阱 The instruction from her supervisor. 借男方自称 supervisor(under my direct supervision)制造干扰，但女方感激的是“认可”而非“上级的指示”，盗用 supervision 一词答非所问。  借用原文：under my direct supervision 

 C) 偷换概念 The honesty of the manager. 中“经理诚实”录音并未作为她感激的内容提及；女方后文虽说 to be perfectly honest，但那是她自述坦率，与“感激经理诚实”无关，属偷换概念。  借用原文：to be perfectly honest

questions.prompt: What has given rise to some complaints about the woman?
options: Her inadequate language proficiency.
Her inability to interact with colleagues properly.
Her inappropriate behavior at company meetings.
Her simplistic approach to dealing with others.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has given rise to some complaints about the woman? 

 【翻译】 什么引发了一些关于女士的投诉? 
 A)  她不足的语言能力。 
 B)  她无法与同事恰当互动。 
 C)  她在公司会议上的不当行为。 
 D)  她对待他人过于简单化的方式。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Her inability to interact with colleagues properly. 
 【定位】 P9 This leads me to the not-so-good part. This mostly centers around one behavioral aspect—your ability to work with others. 
 这就引到不太好的部分了。它主要集中在一个行为方面——你与他人合作的能力。 

 【信号】 转折后才是落点 。男方用 the not-so-good part 把话题从表扬转向批评，这是明确的转向信号；转折之后点出的 your ability to work with others 才是抱怨的真正所指，前半的表扬都是铺垫。 

 【替换】 your ability to work with others ↔ Her inability to interact with colleagues properly. 合作能力即与同事互动 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 Her inadequate language proficiency. 录音从未说她“语言能力不足”；抱怨针对的是 communication style(沟通方式)，与“语言水平”是两回事，属偷换概念。  借用原文：complaints raised about your communication style 

 C) 原词陷阱 Her inappropriate behavior at company meetings. 盗用了 meetings(女方说 we already had like three meetings about this)，但 meetings 是“就此事开过的三次会”，不是“她开会时行为不当”。抱怨的内容是沟通方式，与开会表现无关。  借用原文：we already had like three meetings about this 

 D) 张冠李戴 Her simplistic approach to dealing with others. 借第6段女方自评报告 it's a little simplistic perhaps 里的 simplistic 一词制造干扰，但那句是她评价“这份评估”有点简单，与“她待人方式简单”无关，张冠李戴。  借用原文：it's a little simplistic perhaps

questions.prompt: Why doesn't the woman like to write long emails?
options: To avoid offending the recipients.
To show her unique writing style.
To save time.
To be frank.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why doesn't the woman like to write long emails? 

 【翻译】 女士为什么不喜欢写长邮件? 
 A)  为了避免冒犯收件人。 
 B)  为了展示她独特的写作风格。 
 C)  为了节省时间。 
 D)  为了坦率直接。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） To save time. 
 【定位】 P12 I don't like to write long emails, because, frankly, I think they're a waste of time. Conciseness is efficiency. 
 我不喜欢写长邮件，因为说实话，我觉得那是浪费时间。简洁就是效率。 

 【信号】 因果because直给原因 。她说 I don't like to write long emails, because… I think they're a waste of time，because 之后就是她亲口给出的理由——“浪费时间”，因果信号直白，是最干净的答案句。 

 【替换】 I think they're a waste of time ↔ To save time. 不浪费时间即省时间 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 To avoid offending the recipients. 盗用她说的 it was never my intention to offend anyone，但“无意冒犯”是她对抱怨的辩解，不是她“不写长邮件”的原因。她不写长邮件的理由明确是“浪费时间”，A 答非所问。  借用原文：it was never my intention to offend anyone 

 B) 未提及 To show her unique writing style. 录音从未说她不写长邮件是为“展示独特文风”，纯属凭“写邮件”话题臆造，属未提及。 
 D) 原词陷阱 To be frank. 盗用她话里的 frankly(frankly, I think they're a waste of time) 与 to be perfectly honest，但 frankly 只是她说话的口吻插入语，不是“不写长邮件”的目的。真正原因在 frankly 之后的 a waste of time，D 把语气词错当成了动机。  借用原文：frankly, I think they're a waste of time

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she has always wanted to do since childhood?
options: Provide medical service to the community.
Make healthcare in her hometown the best.
Obtain a doctoral degree in internal medicine.
Have a profound impact on people around her.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say she has always wanted to do since childhood? 

 【翻译】 女士说她从童年起就一直想做什么? 
 A)  为社区提供医疗服务。 
 B)  使她家乡的医疗保健成为最好的。 
 C)  获得内科学博士学位。 
 D)  对周围的人产生深远影响。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Provide medical service to the community. 
 【定位】 P2 As a child, I remember thinking how great it would be to serve the community and cure people! 
 小时候，我就记得自己在想：能服务社区、治病救人该有多好啊！ 

 【信号】 As a child 提示童年愿望 。信号是时间状语 As a child——它直接对应题干的 since childhood，把"从小的愿望"标了出来；紧跟其后的 to serve the community and cure people 就是她从小想做的事。 

 【替换】 serve the community ↔ Provide medical service to the community serve=provide service 
 cure people ↔ medical service cure people 概括为 medical service 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 用了录音里 I come from a small town where healthcare was never the best 中的 healthcare 与"家乡"概念，但录音说的是"家乡医疗从来不算好"，她的愿望是去服务，并没有说要"把家乡医疗变成最好"。这是把原词拼成一个原文没说的目标。  借用原文：I come from a small town where healthcare was never the best 

 C) 未提及 C 说"拿内科博士学位"，但录音里她只说想当医生、想专攻内科，从没提过"博士学位"。这是把后文的 internal medicine 嫁接到一个没出现过的"读博"目标上。 
 D) 与原文相反 D"对身边人产生深远影响"借了录音 that had a profound effect on me 的 profound effect，但原文是"家乡医疗状况对她产生了深远影响"——是别的事影响"她"，不是她要去影响别人。方向被调了个个儿。  借用原文：that had a profound effect on me

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman's parents from the conversation?
options: They have constantly urged her to study hard.
They have worked hard to finance her education.
They have tried to create a positive learning environment.
They have pursued the family's dreams together with her.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the woman's parents from the conversation? 

 【翻译】 从对话中我们对女士的父母了解到什么? 
 A)  他们一直不断督促她努力学习。 
 B)  他们努力工作以资助她的教育。 
 C)  他们试图创造一个积极的学习环境。 
 D)  他们与她一起追求家庭的梦想。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They have constantly urged her to study hard. 
 【定位】 P4 I would certainly say my parents have been a key factor. They always pushed me to study hard. 
 我肯定会说，我父母是关键因素。他们总是督促我努力学习。 

 【信号】 被问者应答里的 my parents 。信号是被问者直接点名 my parents have been a key factor——对话题答案落在回答方，她一提到 parents，下一句 They always pushed me to study hard 就是关于父母的核心信息。 

 【替换】 always pushed me to study hard ↔ constantly urged her to study hard pushed=urged，always=constantly 

 【排除】 B) 偷换概念 B"努力挣钱供她读书"利用了录音 I certainly wouldn't be here without their support 里的 support，但 support 只是泛指"支持"，录音从未说是"经济上出钱（finance）"。这是把一个泛词坐实成具体的金钱资助。  借用原文：I certainly wouldn't be here without their support 

 C) 张冠李戴 C"营造积极学习环境"盗用了录音 a positive environment conducive to my working hard，但说这环境的是"老师、朋友等她周围的人"带来的，原文并没把"营造环境"安在父母头上。这是张冠李戴。  借用原文：surrounded by a positive environment conducive to my working hard 

 D) 未提及 D 说父母"和她一起追求家庭梦想"，录音只说追梦是"她自己的"（pursuing my dreams），并无父母与她"共同追梦"之说。属凭空添加。

questions.prompt: Why does the woman say she wants to choose internal medicine as her specialty?
options: It is a key medical branch conducive to realizing her dreams.
It connects many other specialties with its broad coverage.
It has a long history in the man's prestigious institution.
It is a medical branch both of her parents specialize in.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the woman say she wants to choose internal medicine as her specialty? 

 【翻译】 女士为什么说她想选择内科学作为专业? 
 A)  它是有助于实现她梦想的关键医学分支。 
 B)  它以其广泛的覆盖范围连接许多其他专科。 
 C)  它在男士的知名机构有悠久的历史。 
 D)  它是她父母都专攻的医学分支。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It connects many other specialties with its broad coverage. 
 【定位】 P8 But I find it the most intriguing, because it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties. 
 但我觉得它最有意思，因为它覆盖面很广，又把许多其他专科串联在一起。 

 【信号】 because 领出真正理由 。信号是因果连词 because——它后面 it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties 才是她选内科的真正原因；before because 的 most intriguing 只是感受，理由在 because 之后。 

 【替换】 it covers so much ↔ its broad coverage covers so much=broad coverage 
 ties together so many other specialties ↔ connects many other specialties ties together=connects 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A"有助于实现她的梦想"里的 dreams 确在录音别处出现过（pursuing my dreams），但她解释"为何选内科"时给的理由是"覆盖广、连专科"，从未说内科"有助于实现梦想"。这是把别处的词搬来当本题理由。  借用原文：pursuing my dreams 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 说内科"在这所名校历史悠久"，录音里 prestigious institution（名校）确出现过，但谈的是"学校的声望与竞争"，根本没说内科"历史悠久"。把名校话题硬接到"内科有历史"上。  借用原文：prestigious institution 

 D) 未提及 D"父母都专攻这一科"，录音里父母只"督促她学习"，从没说过父母是医生、更没说专攻内科。这是把 parents 与 internal medicine 两个真词强行拼成一个假关系。

questions.prompt: How does the man describe the woman's school grades?
options: Problematic.
Competitive.
Inconsistent.
Trustworthy.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How does the man describe the woman's school grades? 

 【翻译】 男士如何描述女士的学校成绩? 
 A)  有问题的。 
 B)  有竞争力的。 
 C)  不一致的。 
 D)  值得信赖的。 

 【答案】 C （态度观点题） Inconsistent. 
 【定位】 P11 You do get top grades here and there, but you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"? 
 你确实这儿那儿拿过一些顶尖成绩，但你不太……怎么说呢，"稳定"？ 

 【信号】 转折 but 后才是真评价 。信号是转折词 but——but 之前的 You do get top grades 是先扬，but 之后 you are not very… consistent 才是男方真正的评价：成绩不够稳定。态度题的落点在转折后。 

 【替换】 you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"? ↔ Inconsistent not consistent=inconsistent 
 a bit of a mixed bag ↔ Inconsistent mixed bag=时好时坏=inconsistent 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A"有问题的"借了录音 I see no problem in making you a conditional offer 里的 problem，但那句说的是"给你有条件录取没问题"，是对"录取"说的，不是评价成绩"有问题"。盗了 problem 却换了对象。  借用原文：I see no problem in making you a conditional offer 

 B) 张冠李戴 B"有竞争力的"盗用录音 a highly competitive and promising student body 的 competitive，但那是男方夸"本校生源竞争激烈"，与"她的成绩"无关。张冠李戴到了成绩头上。  借用原文：a highly competitive and promising student body 

 D) 与原文相反 D"可信赖的"是褒义，但男方对成绩的整体态度是负面的（mixed bag、not consistent、warned），方向完全相反。把先扬后抑听成了纯表扬。  借用原文：consider yourself warned

questions.prompt: Why do we often have to choose photos that include a street sign to log into our email accounts?
options: To prevent hackers from cracking our secret codes.
To show that all the guidelines are being followed.
To provide evidence that passwords are forgotten.
To convince our computer that we are human.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why do we often have to choose photos that include a street sign to log into our email accounts? 

 【翻译】 为什么我们在登录电子邮件账户时经常需要选择包含街道标志的照片? 
 A)  防止黑客破解我们的密码。 
 B)  表明所有准则都得到遵守。 
 C)  提供密码被遗忘的证据。 
 D)  使我们的计算机相信我们是人类。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） To convince our computer that we are human. 
 【定位】 P1 More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being. 
 你往往还得去选那些含有街道标志的照片，因为这显然能向你的电脑提供确凿的证据，证明你其实是一个人类。 

 【信号】 原因信号 as 引出真意 。答案就在 as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being 里的 as 之后——as 在这里是『因为』，专门交代前面『选含街道标志照片』这个动作的目的，是典型的原因信号。 

 【替换】 provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being ↔ To convince our computer that we are human 提供证据=使信服，同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项里的 hackers 让人联想原文开头 hack into the Pentagon，但那只是开篇打比方说登录难，与『选街道标志照片是为了什么』无关，属听到 hack 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：trying to hack into the Pentagon 

 B) 原词陷阱 all the guidelines are being followed 借用原文 If you follow all of the guidelines，但原文那句是在罗列守规则有多麻烦，并非解释选照片的目的，词对了、对应错了。  借用原文：If you follow all of the guidelines 

 C) 未提及 passwords are forgotten 把后文『人会忘密码』这个话题硬塞进本题，但选照片是为了证明你是人，跟『提供忘记密码的证据』毫无关系，原文也没这么说。

questions.prompt: What do researchers at a university in Finland aim to do in their new study?
options: Put an end to the hacking phenomenon.
Help people remember their passwords.
Reduce the intricacy of the password itself.
Explain the need for different email accounts.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do researchers at a university in Finland aim to do in their new study? 

 【翻译】 芬兰一所大学的研究人员在他们的新研究中旨在做什么? 
 A)  终结黑客攻击现象。 
 B)  帮助人们记住他们的密码。 
 C)  降低密码本身的复杂性。 
 D)  解释不同电子邮件账户的必要性。 

 【答案】 B （目的题） Help people remember their passwords. 
 【定位】 P2 Now a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon. 
 如今，芬兰阿尔托大学研究者开展的一项新的同行评审研究，正试图弄清我们为什么会忘记密码，以期帮助终结这一令人沮丧的现象。 

 【信号】 目的信号 in order to help 。研究者的真正目标由 in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon 中的 in order to 引出——in order to 是直白的目的信号，它后面才是研究的最终意图。 

 【替换】 help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon ↔ Help people remember their passwords 代词 this 指回忘密码，概括等值 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Put an end to the hacking phenomenon 直接搬原文 put an end to this frustrating phenomenon 的 put an end to，却把对象偷换成 hacking（黑客）；原文要终结的是『忘密码』这一令人沮丧的现象，不是黑客现象。  借用原文：in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon 

 C) 原词陷阱 Reduce the intricacy of the password itself 借了原文反复出现的 the password itself，但研究的发现是『记不记得住与密码本身关系不大』，从未说要降低密码复杂度，是把原词拼成原文没有的目标。  借用原文：less to do with the password itself 

 D) 原词陷阱 Explain the need for different email accounts 让人想到原文 a different password for every one of your accounts，但那是开篇讲守规则的麻烦，与芬兰研究的目标无关，accounts 这个词被挪用来骗选。  借用原文：a different password for every one of your accounts

questions.prompt: What do the researchers advise websites to do at the end of the passage?
options: Innovate technologies to ensure the safety of users' accounts.
Provide incentives for the application of creative passwords.
Explore the possibility of using simpler secret codes.
Take steps to encourage users to log in more often.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do the researchers advise websites to do at the end of the passage? 

 【翻译】 研究人员在文章末尾建议网站做什么? 
 A)  创新技术以确保用户账户的安全。 
 B)  为使用创造性密码提供激励。 
 C)  探索使用更简单密码的可能性。 
 D)  采取措施鼓励用户更频繁地登录。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Take steps to encourage users to log in more often. 
 【定位】 P2 The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often in order to help them remember their secret codes. 
 研究者建议网站多设置一些激励，促使用户更频繁地登录，以帮助他们记住自己的密码。 

 【信号】 建议信号 advise 直接给出对策 。答案由 The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often 里的 advise 直接引出——advise 是建议信号，它后面 websites to... 的内容就是研究者给出的对策。 

 【替换】 include more of an incentive for users to log in more often ↔ Take steps to encourage users to log in more often 设激励=采取措施鼓励，同义改写 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 Innovate technologies to ensure the safety of users' accounts 蹭全篇的安全 / accounts 话题，但研究者的建议是加登录激励，从未让网站去『创新技术保障账户安全』，是凭话题耳熟编出的拔高项。 
 B) 原词陷阱 Provide incentives for the application of creative passwords 直接搬原文 include more of an incentive 的 incentive，最易骗『听到 incentive 就选』，但原文是为『更常登录』设激励，不是为『使用创意密码』，对象被偷换了。  借用原文：include more of an incentive for users to log in more often 

 C) 原词陷阱 Explore the possibility of using simpler secret codes 借了原文结尾的 secret codes，但原文那句是说激励的目的（帮人记住密码），研究者并没建议用更简单的密码，词对、意思不对。  借用原文：help them remember their secret codes

questions.prompt: What was the problem Jenny Weiner encountered four years ago?
options: Her work no longer interested her.
Her training app did not fit her.
Her fitness fell into a slump.
Her business deteriorated.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What was the problem Jenny Weiner encountered four years ago? 

 【翻译】 四年前Jenny Weiner遇到了什么问题? 
 A)  她的工作不再让她感兴趣。 
 B)  她的训练应用程序不适合她。 
 C)  她的健身状况陷入低迷。 
 D)  她的生意恶化了。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Her fitness fell into a slump. 
 【定位】 P1 Four years ago, Jenny Weiner was in a fitness slump. 
 四年前，珍妮·韦纳的健身状态陷入了低谷。 

 【信号】 开篇点题句 + 与题干 four years ago 时间对齐 。录音开头 Four years ago, Jenny Weiner was in a fitness slump. 的时间状语 four years ago 与题干完全对齐，是篇章开篇交代背景的点题句，承载本题答案。 

 【替换】 in a fitness slump ↔ Her fitness fell into a slump. 同词换句式：介词短语改写成主谓句，核心词 fitness slump 不变 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Her work no longer interested her. 说的是 "工作不再有趣"，但录音通篇只谈健身、训练 app，从未提及她的 work 或兴趣转变，属凭常识脑补的未提及项。 
 B) 原词陷阱 Her training app did not fit her. 借用了原文反复出现的 training 与 app，可录音里 She then discovered the fitness phone app Slimmeretics. 表明 app 是她发现后用来解决问题的工具，并非四年前遇到的问题本身，听到 app 就选正中圈套。  借用原文：She then discovered the fitness phone app Slimmeretics. 

 D) 偷换概念 Her business deteriorated. 把 "健身低谷" 偷换成 "生意变差"，business 与原文 fitness slump 词形相近、都是 "某事变糟" 的格局，但录音谈的是身体健身状态而非商业，方向被悄悄换掉。

questions.prompt: What can the fitness phone app Slimmeretics do according to the passage?
options: Help users keep track of their fitness levels.
Design personalised training programmes.
Strengthen ties among users worldwide.
Select well-qualified human coaches.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What can the fitness phone app Slimmeretics do according to the passage? 

 【翻译】 根据文章,健身手机应用程序Slimmeretics能做什么? 
 A)  帮助用户跟踪他们的健身水平。 
 B)  设计个性化的训练方案。 
 C)  加强全球用户之间的联系。 
 D)  挑选资质优秀的真人教练。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Design personalised training programmes. 
 【定位】 P1 A virtual coach then uses that information to suggest a personalised training regime. 
 随后一个虚拟教练会利用这些信息，推荐一套个性化的训练方案。 

 【信号】 功能描述句：suggest 引出 app 提供的核心服务 。A virtual coach then uses that information to suggest a personalised training regime. 用 suggest（推荐/给出）这一动作直接交代了 app 的核心功能——量身定制训练方案，是承载本题答案的功能描述句。 

 【替换】 suggest a personalised training regime ↔ Design personalised training programmes. 近义词替换：suggest→Design、regime→programmes，personalised 原样保留 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Help users keep track of their fitness levels. 看似贴合 app 的智能形象，且原文确有 gives feedback 与 adjust future training sessions 这类近似 "追踪/调整" 的表述，但原文说的是据反馈调整训练，从未说帮用户 "记录健身水平"，是借相近语境编出的功能。  借用原文：the app's artificial intelligence software system gives feedback 

 C) 原词陷阱 Strengthen ties among users worldwide. 借用了原文 its other 53 million users around the world 里 "全球用户" 的字眼，可原文只是说 app 收集这些用户的反馈来优化训练，根本没提让用户彼此 "加强联系"，听到 worldwide users 就选会掉坑。  借用原文：its other 53 million users around the world 

 D) 原词陷阱 Select well-qualified human coaches. 借用原文反复出现的 human personal trainers/coach，可原文明说 app 配的是 A virtual coach（虚拟教练），并非 app 去挑选真人教练；末尾还有专家称 apps cannot replace human personal trainers，方向恰相反。  借用原文：A virtual coach then uses that information

questions.prompt: Why does the passage say Jenny Weiner now finds the workouts exciting?
options: They are never repeated.
They help enrich her life.
They are of no extreme intensity.
They keep her focused on her goal.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the passage say Jenny Weiner now finds the workouts exciting? 

 【翻译】 文章为什么说Jenny Weiner现在觉得锻炼令人兴奋? 
 A)  它们从不重复。 
 B)  它们有助于丰富她的生活。 
 C)  它们的强度不是极高的。 
 D)  它们让她专注于自己的目标。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They are never repeated. 
 【定位】 P1 Now Ms. Weiner finds the workouts exciting. This is because no two are ever the same. 
 如今韦纳女士觉得训练很有意思。这是因为没有任何两次训练是相同的。 

 【信号】 因果信号 This is because 紧跟其后的句子即原因 。原文先说她觉得训练有趣，紧接 This is because no two are ever the same. 用因果信号 This is because 引出原因——没有两次训练是一样的，正是本题答案落点。 

 【替换】 no two are ever the same ↔ They are never repeated. 肯否结构转换："没有两次相同" = "从不重复"，意思等值 

 【排除】 B) 答非所问 They help enrich her life. 听来正面、也像 app 的好处，但题问的是 "为何觉得训练 exciting"，原文给的原因明确是 no two are ever the same，而非 "丰富生活"；该项答的是别的问题。 
 C) 原词陷阱 They are of no extreme intensity. 借用了原文 her workouts lacked intensity 中的 intensity，可那句讲的是四年前训练缺乏强度的旧问题，与 "现在为何觉得有趣" 无关，听到 intensity 就选即中招。  借用原文：her workouts lacked intensity 

 D) 原词陷阱 They keep her focused on her goal. 借用原文 your desired goals 里的 goal，可原文谈 goal 只是说输入资料时填写目标，并未把 "专注目标" 说成她觉得训练有趣的原因，原因仍是 no two are ever the same。  借用原文：your desired goals

questions.prompt: What do some experts think of fitness apps like Slimmeretics?
options: They will not be able to take the place of human personal trainers.
They will not be able to comprehend some of the profiles users put in.
They cannot lead to optimal results with their mathematical approach.
They cannot match humans in arranging meticulous workout schedules.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do some experts think of fitness apps like Slimmeretics? 

 【翻译】 一些专家如何看待像Slimmeretics这样的健身应用程序? 
 A)  它们无法取代真人私人教练。 
 B)  它们无法理解用户输入的某些个人资料。 
 C)  它们无法通过数学方法达到最佳效果。 
 D)  它们在安排细致的锻炼计划方面无法与人类相比。 

 【答案】 A （态度观点题） They will not be able to take the place of human personal trainers. 
 【定位】 P1 However, some experts think that apps cannot replace human personal trainers. 
 然而，一些专家认为这些 app 无法取代真人私人教练。 

 【信号】 转折 However + 评价主体 some experts 直接表态 。原文前面一直夸 app 效果好，However, some experts think that apps cannot replace human personal trainers. 用转折 However 转向、并由评价主体 some experts 直陈观点，转折后才是本题真意。 

 【替换】 apps cannot replace human personal trainers ↔ They will not be able to take the place of human personal trainers. 近义短语替换：replace = take the place of，human personal trainers 原样保留 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 They will not be able to comprehend some of the profiles users put in. 借用了原文 It will not comprehend that there are competing interests 的 comprehend，以及输入环节的 profile，可原文说 app 不能理解的是 "人类行为/相互竞争的利益"，而非看不懂用户填的 profiles，对象被偷换。  借用原文：It will not comprehend that there are competing interests outside of health and fitness. 

 C) 与原文相反 They cannot lead to optimal results with their mathematical approach. 盗用了原文 mathematical approach 与 optimal results，可原文是正面说 The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule. This has led to optimal results.——数学方法"能"带来最优结果，选项加了 cannot 把极性反了。  借用原文：The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule. This has led to optimal results. 

 D) 与原文相反 They cannot match humans in arranging meticulous workout schedules. 借用原文 meticulous workout schedule，可原文是正面称 The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule.——app 能编排更精细的计划，并非说它在这点上不如真人，方向相反。  借用原文：The app's mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule.

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the conclusion of the Oxford University researchers?
options: All societies are built upon the cornerstones of basic values.
Everyone everywhere demonstrates seven character traits.
All societies are kept together by seven basic moral rules.
Everyone everywhere shares a universal moral standard.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the conclusion of the Oxford University researchers? 

 【翻译】 我们从牛津大学研究人员的结论中了解到什么？ 
 A)  所有社会都建立在基本价值观的基石之上。 
 B)  各地的每个人都展现出七种性格特征。 
 C)  所有社会都由七条基本道德规则维系在一起。 
 D)  各地的每个人都有共同的普世道德标准。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） All societies are kept together by seven basic moral rules. 
 【定位】 P1 All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded. 
 牛津大学得出结论：所有社会都靠七条普世道德规则维系在一起，其中包括服从尊长、尊重他人财物。 

 【信号】 结论标志词 concluded 。句末的 Oxford University has concluded 是明确的结论信号，加之这句出现在篇章开头点题处，正是篇章独白把核心论点摆在开头的典型位置，听到 concluded 就该锁定这句是答案句。 

 【替换】 All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules ↔ All societies are kept together by seven basic moral rules held together 同义改写为 kept together 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 All societies are built upon the cornerstones of basic values. 把第一段后文的 basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies 的原词 cornerstones、basic values 搬了过来，但那句讲的是成功社会的基石，并非研究的总结论本身，听到熟词就选会落进这个陷阱。  借用原文：basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies 

 B) 偷换概念 Everyone everywhere demonstrates seven character traits. 借了原文出现过的 seven 和第二段的 The character traits held for every kind of community，但研究的结论说的是七条道德规则（rules），而非七种性格特质，把 rules 偷换成 character traits 就跑偏了。  借用原文：The character traits held for every kind of community 

 D) 偷换概念 Everyone everywhere shares a universal moral standard. 用了第二段 Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code 的熟悉句式，但原文说的是共享一套七条规则的道德准则（code），D 把它笼统说成 a universal moral standard，丢掉了结论里七条规则这一核心，不如 C 精确对应题干问的结论。  借用原文：Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code

questions.prompt: What did the new study by Oxford researchers aim to do?
options: Ascertain whether deferring to authority was confined to right-wing people.
Find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.
Make clear whether all societies faced the same moral issues.
Find out whether left-wing people still had a group loyalty.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the new study by Oxford researchers aim to do? 

 【翻译】 牛津研究人员的新研究旨在做什么？ 
 A)  确定服从权威是否仅限于右翼人士。 
 B)  查明不同社会是否有不同版本的道德观。 
 C)  弄清所有社会是否面临相同的道德问题。 
 D)  查明左翼人士是否仍然具有群体忠诚。 

 【答案】 B （目的题） Find out whether different societies had different versions of morality. 
 【定位】 P3 The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality. 
 这项发表于《当代人类学》的研究是有史以来规模最大、最全面、覆盖最广的道德调查，旨在弄清不同社会是否有不同版本的道德观。 

 【信号】 意图标志 aimed to find out 。句中的 aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality 用 aimed to 直陈研究目的，这是目的题最直接的信号，听到 aimed to 即可锁定。 

 【替换】 aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality ↔ Find out whether different societies had different versions of morality 近乎原句，仅去掉 aimed to 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Ascertain whether deferring to authority was confined to right-wing people. 把第二段 Dr. Curry 那句里的 deferring to authority 和 right-wing 原词搬来，但那是他举例说明规则的普世性，并非这项研究本身要弄清的目标，听到熟词就选会被带偏。  借用原文：deferring to authority 

 C) 偷换概念 Make clear whether all societies faced the same moral issues. 听上去和研究目的沾边，但原文目的是查不同社会是否有不同版本的道德，C 反向说成所有社会是否面对相同道德问题，方向被改了。  借用原文：whether different societies had different versions of morality 

 D) 原词陷阱 Find out whether left-wing people still had a group loyalty. 借了第二段 left-wing people will still have a group loyalty 的原话，但那是 Dr. Curry 论证规则普世性的例子，不是研究要查明的目标，属典型的盗用原句却答非所问。  借用原文：left-wing people will still have a group loyalty

questions.prompt: What does Harvey Whitehouse think social scientists should do to theories of morality?
options: Make independent descriptions of cultures around the world.
Strive to understand the basic differences between peoples.
Appreciate the foundational value of the existing data.
Carry out systematic field studies to gather new data.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does Harvey Whitehouse think social scientists should do to theories of morality? 

 【翻译】 Harvey Whitehouse认为社会科学家应该如何对待道德理论？ 
 A)  对世界各地的文化进行独立描述。 
 B)  努力理解不同民族之间的基本差异。 
 C)  认识到现有数据的基础价值。 
 D)  开展系统的实地研究以收集新数据。 

 【答案】 D （目的题） Carry out systematic field studies to gather new data. 
 【定位】 P3 In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field. 
 今后，社会科学家若真要检验道德理论，就需要更系统地到实地去采集新数据。 

 【信号】 建议信号 will need to + 转折 rather than 。Whitehouse 先说 should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data，再用 they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field 点明做法；need to 是建议信号，rather than relying on old data 则用对比把落点推向新数据。 

 【替换】 gather new data, more systematically, out in the field ↔ Carry out systematic field studies to gather new data. systematically 名词化、out in the field 转为 field studies 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Make independent descriptions of cultures around the world. 搬了原文 These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing 的原词 independent、descriptions，但那是在说本研究所依据的旧资料的来历，不是 Whitehouse 主张今后该做的事，时间方向相反。  借用原文：These descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we're testing 

 B) 张冠李戴 Strive to understand the basic differences between peoples. 借了第三段 Dr. Curry 那句 appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ 的差异话题，但那是 Curry 的期望，且题干问的是 Whitehouse 的主张，张冠李戴又跑了题。  借用原文：appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ 

 C) 与原文相反 Appreciate the foundational value of the existing data. 里的 existing data 恰是 Whitehouse 用 rather than relying on old data 明确否定的对象，他主张采集新数据，C 取了被否定的旧数据一侧，方向反了。  借用原文：rather than relying on old data

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about our eyes?
options: They might be the most important part of our eating experience.
They can activate our brain functions in a most direct fashion.
They can be viewed as the windows to our soul.
They could mislead us in more ways than one.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about our eyes? 

 【翻译】 讲话者关于我们的眼睛说了什么? 
 A)  它们可能是我们进食体验中最重要的部分。 
 B)  它们能够以最直接的方式激活我们的大脑功能。 
 C)  它们可以被视为我们心灵的窗户。 
 D)  它们可能以不止一种方式误导我们。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They might be the most important part of our eating experience. 
 【定位】 P2 For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience. 
 尽管人们老在谈论舌头（的味觉），我们的眼睛或许才真正是吃这件事里最重要的部分。 

 【信号】 让步 For all… + 强调 really might 。信号是句首让步结构 For all the talk of the tongue（"尽管都在说舌头"）后面才抛出真正主张，再加 our eyes really might be the most important part 里的 "really" 加重语气——让步之后、被强调的那句才是说话人的落点，正是答案句。 

 【替换】 our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience ↔ They might be the most important part of our eating experience. 近乎原句、They 替 our eyes 

 【排除】 B) 偷换概念 B 盗用了第 2 段原词 brain functions。原文说 A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision——是 "很多脑功能用于处理视觉"，主语是脑功能、用来佐证 eyes 重要；B 把它倒过来说成 "眼睛激活脑功能"，还加了原文没有的 "in a most direct fashion"，是偷换概念，且没回答 "说话人对 eyes 的核心论断"。  借用原文：A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision 

 C) 未提及 C 借用了关于眼睛的常见俗语 "心灵的窗户"，听着像常识、最易顺口选中，但整篇录音只把眼睛和 "eating experience（吃的体验）" 挂钩，从未说眼睛是 "心灵的窗户"，属原文未提及，凭常识选它就中招。 
 D) 与原文相反 D 说眼睛会 mislead us（误导我们），是贬义。但答案句对眼睛是高度肯定——our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience，说话人在抬高眼睛而非贬低。D 的态度与原文相反，故排除。  借用原文：our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience

questions.prompt: What does color actually do according to this lecture?
options: It attracts food companies' growing attention.
It adversely impacts one's eating experience.
It invariably determines how food sells.
It changes the way people taste food.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does color actually do according to this lecture? 

 【翻译】 根据这次讲座,颜色实际上起什么作用? 
 A)  它吸引了食品公司日益增长的关注。 
 B)  它对一个人的进食体验产生负面影响。 
 C)  它总是决定食品的销售情况。 
 D)  它改变了人们品尝食物的方式。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It changes the way people taste food. 
 【定位】 P2 And the result is that color actually changes how we taste food. 
 其结果就是，颜色实际上改变了我们品尝食物的方式。 

 【信号】 结果词 the result is + actually 。信号是因果收束词 the result is that（"其结果是"）领出全段结论，又叠加 color actually changes how we taste food 里的 "actually"，与题干 "actually do" 直接呼应——结果句 + actually 强调，这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 color actually changes how we taste food ↔ It changes the way people taste food. how we taste = the way people taste 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 A 盗用第 1 段背景里的 "food companies"。原文确说 Food companies know that better color gives better prices，但那是讲公司在意颜色的背景，不是回答 "color actually do（颜色实际起什么作用）"；且原文是公司已经关注，A 说 "growing attention（关注在增长）" 也无依据，属答非所问。  借用原文：Food companies know that better color gives better prices 

 B) 与原文相反 B 借 eating experience 这个原文反复出现的词（第 2 段就有 the eating experience），却安上 "adversely impacts（负面影响）"。原文从头到尾把颜色讲成 "改变味觉、帮助判断" 的中性甚至有用的作用，从没说颜色 "负面影响" 吃的体验，态度相反，排除。  借用原文：the most important part of the eating experience 

 C) 过度推断 C 盗用第 1 段 "color is money / better prices" 的卖钱话题，推成 It invariably determines how food sells.。原文只说 better color gives better prices（更好的颜色卖更好的价），是 "有助于"，C 用绝对词 "invariably（无一例外地决定）" 把话说死，超出原文，属过度推断。  借用原文：better color gives better prices

questions.prompt: What does the brain use color to do?
options: Enhance the taste.
Make predictions.
Identify distinct flavors.
Enrich the eating experience.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the brain use color to do? 

 【翻译】 大脑利用颜色做什么? 
 A)  增强味道。 
 B)  做出预测。 
 C)  识别不同的风味。 
 D)  丰富进食体验。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Make predictions. 
 【定位】 P3 The brain makes predictions using color. 
 大脑利用颜色来做出预测。 

 【信号】 brain + color 同现的机制句 。信号是录音第一次把 The brain 和 using color 放进同一句、直接给出动作的机制句 The brain makes predictions using color——题干问 "大脑用颜色做什么"，正是这句把主语、工具、动作三者一次说全，即答案句。 

 【替换】 The brain makes predictions using color ↔ Make predictions. makes predictions = Make predictions 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 说 Enhance the taste.（增强味道），听着像 "颜色让吃更好" 的常识，但录音讲的是颜色让大脑做预测、形成对甜/酸的预期，从没说颜色 "增强" 味道本身，属原文未提及。 
 C) 张冠李戴 C 盗用第 3 段实验里的原词 "identify the flavor"。原文 each of them identified the orange flavor 说的是 "实验参与者借助看到颜色去辨认味道"，是讲颜色影响味觉的证据；题问的是 "大脑用颜色做什么"，答案是 "做预测"，C 把实验现象当成大脑机制本身，属张冠李戴、答非所问。  借用原文：each of them identified the orange flavor 

 D) 未提及 D 说 Enrich the eating experience.（丰富吃的体验），借用了贯穿全篇的 "eating experience" 话题词，但原文说大脑用颜色是去 "做预测、形成味觉预期"，从没说颜色用来 "丰富" 吃的体验，属原文未提及。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say many of us search for throughout our lives?
options: Social status.
Financial resources.
Meaning.
Happiness.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say many of us search for throughout our lives? 

 【翻译】 说话人说我们许多人终其一生都在寻找什么? 
 A)  社会地位。 
 B)  经济资源。 
 C)  意义。 
 D)  幸福。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Meaning. 
 【定位】 P1 Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives. 
 追寻意义，是我们许多人一生中都会经历的事。 

 【信号】 开篇点题句即答案 。录音第一句 Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives 与题干 throughout our lives 逐词呼应，是典型的‘开篇点题’信号——篇章独白常把核心对象放在第一句领出，这里把 meaning 摆在句首作主语，正是答案所在。 

 【替换】 Searching for meaning ↔ Meaning 动名词短语取其宾语名词 

 【排除】 D) 原词陷阱 录音紧接着说 having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness，happiness 在这里是‘意义带来的结果’，不是‘人们追寻的东西’。选项 Happiness 盗用了这个刚听到的原词，但答非所问——题目问的是 search for 的对象。  借用原文：having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness 

 B) 原词陷阱 in the context of financial resources 里 financial resources 是这项研究的考察背景/变量，全篇没说它是‘人们一生追寻的东西’。选项 Financial resources 盗用了后文反复出现的财富一词来诱选。  借用原文：in the context of financial resources 

 A) 未提及 For some, this meaning is religious, some political and some interpersonal 列举的是意义的种类（宗教、政治、人际），通篇并未把 social status（社会地位）说成人们追寻的东西，属无中生有。

questions.prompt: What do Rhia Catapano and colleagues find about economic resources?
options: Their effect on people's happiness has long been overstated.
Their influence on people's life varies with social contexts.
They can affect people's experience of meaning.
They can ensure people's overall well-being.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do Rhia Catapano and colleagues find about economic resources? 

 【翻译】 Rhia Catapano及其同事关于经济资源有什么发现? 
 A)  经济资源对人们幸福感的影响长期以来被夸大了。 
 B)  经济资源对人们生活的影响因社会环境而异。 
 C)  经济资源能够影响人们对意义的体验。 
 D)  经济资源能够确保人们的整体幸福。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They can affect people's experience of meaning. 
 【定位】 P2 Rhea Catapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people, suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning. 
 多伦多大学的 Rhea Catapano 及其同事发现，对富人而言，意义对幸福的预测作用远弱于穷人，这表明经济资源会影响我们体验意义的方式。 

 【信号】 find…suggesting 引出结论 。录音用 find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness…suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning 把研究结论端出来：动词 find 直接对应题干的 find，而 suggesting 之后那半句正是对‘经济资源起什么作用’的定性回答，是结论信号最集中处。 

 【替换】 economic resources can impact how we experience meaning ↔ They can affect people's experience of meaning impact=affect 同义替换 
 economic resources ↔ They 代词回指经济资源 

 【排除】 D) 偷换概念 录音说财富影响的是 how we experience meaning（体验意义的方式），并未说它能‘保证整体幸福’。选项 They can ensure people's overall well-being 借用了全篇高频词 happiness 的近义概念 well-being，还把‘影响’夸大成‘保证（ensure）’，对象与程度都改了。  借用原文：economic resources can impact how we experience meaning 

 A) 未提及 meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people 谈的是‘穷富之间预测力强弱不同’，从未说‘财富对幸福的影响被长期夸大’。选项 Their effect on people's happiness has long been overstated 凭空造出一个‘被夸大’的评价，是无中生有，正应了预读对 overstated 这个程度词的预警。 
 B) 原词陷阱 录音说差异取决于 income（收入高低），而非 social contexts（社会环境）。第三项研究里虽有 social ladder（社会阶梯）一词，但那是测量财富地位的工具，不是‘随社会环境而变’。选项 Their influence on people's life varies with social contexts 盗用了 social 这个原词来制造熟悉感。  借用原文：they placed themselves on a "social ladder"

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Rhia Catapano and colleagues' second study?
options: It used questions totally different from those in their first study.
It focused on the sense of meaning of French participants.
It analysed cases from a daily poll of US residents.
It examined data collected from multiple countries.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about Rhia Catapano and colleagues' second study? 

 【翻译】 关于Rhia Catapano及其同事的第二项研究,我们了解到什么? 
 A)  该研究使用的问题与他们第一项研究中的问题完全不同。 
 B)  该研究聚焦于法国参与者的意义感。 
 C)  该研究分析了来自美国居民每日民意调查的案例。 
 D)  该研究检验了从多个国家收集的数据。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It examined data collected from multiple countries. 
 【定位】 P2 The second study looked at worldwide data. 
 第二项研究考察的是全球范围的数据。 

 【信号】 序数词 second 直接定位 。录音用序数词把三项研究串起来：first study…second study…final study。题干问 second study，就听 The second study looked at worldwide data 这句——worldwide data（全球数据）是这项研究区别于前后两项的核心特征，序数词是最干净的定位信号。 

 【替换】 worldwide data ↔ data collected from multiple countries worldwide=multiple countries 

 【排除】 C) 张冠李戴 The first study used data from a daily poll of US residents 明说‘分析美国居民每日民调’的是第一项研究，不是第二项。选项 It analysed cases from a daily poll of US residents 盗用了 daily poll of US residents 这串原话，但安到了错的研究上。  借用原文：The first study used data from a daily poll of US residents 

 B) 张冠李戴 In the final study, French participants indicated 表明‘聚焦法国被试’的是最终那项研究，而非第二项。选项 It focused on the sense of meaning of French participants 盗用 French participants 这一原词，错配到第二项研究上。  借用原文：In the final study, French participants indicated 

 A) 与原文相反 录音说第二项研究 Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study，幸福度用的是与第一项‘相同’的问题；选项 It used questions totally different from those in their first study 恰好把 same（相同）反说成 totally different（全然不同），正话反说。  借用原文：Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study

questions.prompt: Why do meaning and happiness have a weaker relationship in those with more resources?
options: They might have more access to external sources of happiness.
They might focus on an individual sense of satisfaction or meaning.
They might be less easily affected by a community's overall feeling.
They might be less adversely impacted by failure to achieve a purpose.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why do meaning and happiness have a weaker relationship in those with more resources? 

 【翻译】 为什么在拥有更多资源的人群中,意义和幸福之间的关系更弱? 
 A)  他们可能有更多途径获得外部幸福来源。 
 B)  他们可能更关注个人的满足感或意义感。 
 C)  他们可能较少受到群体整体情绪的影响。 
 D)  他们可能较少受到未能实现目标的负面影响。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They might have more access to external sources of happiness. 
 【定位】 P3 This might be the case because rich individuals have more access to other sources of happiness—many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community. 
 之所以如此，可能是因为富人能接触到更多其他的幸福来源——其中许多是外部的，比如没有压力、或拥有社群。 

 【信号】 because 引出原因 。录音用 This might be the case because rich individuals have more access to other sources of happiness 给出解释，because 是最直接的因果信号，其后那句正是‘富人为何关系更弱’的答案；后面 many of which will be external 进一步点明这些来源是‘外部的’。
